title: Joshua Báez hits two home runs in Triple-A game for Cardinals affiliate
text:
St. Louis’ offense is experiencing an increase in scoring, contributing to the team’s strong start this season, according to a May 27 report. However, the Cardinals have struggled to get offensive production from their outfielders apart from Jordan Walker, with the group collectively hitting .220/.265/.331.
At Triple-A, prospect Joshua Báez is showing signs of improvement while playing center field. Báez recorded his first multihomer game of the season and matched career highs with four hits and five RBIs during a 19-5 win over Omaha at Werner Park. The performance was part of a recent surge in power for Báez, who has hit seven extra-base hits—including five home runs—in his last 11 at-bats over a ten-day span. This stretch has increased his OPS by 74 points to .852, marking his highest point this season.
Báez is ranked as MLB’s No. 68 prospect and now has 13 home runs on the year, tying him with teammate Jimmy Crooks for third place in the International League. He also holds a hard-hit rate of 49.1 percent, placing him in the 86th percentile among players at the Triple-A level.
During Tuesday’s game against Omaha, Báez had three batted balls exceeding 103 mph exit velocity. His day began with a single hit at 104.9 mph off pitcher Mitch Spence before hitting two home runs off Spence’s breaking pitches—one traveling at an exit velocity of 94.5 mph and another at 103.9 mph.
Despite improvements in power numbers since last year’s breakout season—which included reducing his strikeout rate from 35.5 percent to 20.6—Báez’s strikeout rate has risen again this year to approximately 33 percent, and he continues to face challenges against higher velocity pitching.
